**83** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/README.md`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/credential-resolver.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 47 pages)`, `/automation/:name (route, 45 pages)`
- **32** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cbc90bb2a0235b681e734fe8e03bd88c241b9421` — the merge of head `26a79e38acbcac329a829db2c5c30504959a920e` into base `c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cbc90bb2a0235b681e734fe8e03bd88c241b9421 && git checkout cbc90bb2a0235b681e734fe8e03bd88c241b9421
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22 26a79e38acbcac329a829db2c5c30504959a920e && git checkout -B drift-repro c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22 && git merge --no-ff 26a79e38acbcac329a829db2c5c30504959a920e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c5d46341747746b180626ad2fcb918324341cd22` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The `status` doc ("a stored value stays `rejected` across a restart until a provider proves it … a call answered `2xx` does not clear it") matches `markVerified`/`markCallAccepted`.

**packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts** — the marker's docblock says the materializer "does not retry it on a timer: the next attempt is the next change of the credential". On the head that is true only of a stored or declaration-written value; an env/vault value IS retried on the backoff (`holdConnectorForRejectedCredential`, non-held branch; ADR note says so). should-fix: qualify the sentence ("when the value is a stored one"), since this docblock ships in `dist` and is what a provider author reads. The class itself holds: structural check, `cause` assignment identical to the sibling, status carried.

**packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts** — `credentialVerified` doc and consumer agree. Tried to break: an `mcp` instance with `auth: none` and a literal token in `providerConfig.transport.headers` reports no `credentialVerified` (right — nothing of ours was proved) and on a 401 is held as a declaration-written credential (`credential === undefined`), which the ADR note states. Holds.

**packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts** — holds; derived set follows; censuses regenerated.

**skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md** — against the spec it teaches on `main` and the skill's eval. The new sentence is true of the head: env wins (`envValue` first), the PUT route exists and is `manage_metadata`-gated, and an unset ref degrades the instance "until set" (`degradeConnectorForCredential` + reconcile on `object:revision`). `SKILL.md:404` ("the customer's administrator supplies the value") still holds. The skill's own eval, `skills/objectstack-automation/evals/integrations-declared.json` case 2 (Stripe `GetBalance`), still grades toward "the administrator sets `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` on the deployment, an unset ref fails boot" — the recipe now teaches the opposite; `must_contain` does not pin the sentence, so no gate moved, but a grader reading the expected output will mark a correct answer wrong on that point. should-fix: realign the eval prose in the same change as the recipe. Token ratchet: green in Lint & Repo Gates.

**Cross-cutting should-fixes read in the cited code (not `hits`, named for the lane):**

A `basic` password travels as base64(`username:value`) in `Authorization`; an `api-key` with `paramName` travels URL-encoded in the request URL (which an SDK error, and the mcp `${err.message}` tail, can carry). An upstream or SDK message echoing either form passes the scrub into `status_reason`, the husk reason and the log `meta`. should-fix: also withhold `encodeURIComponent(value)` and the base64 forms.
- An env/vault refusal (`credentialRefusals`) is reported `rejected` until restart, an `mcp` proof, or a source change — even after the instance re-materializes and serves `2xx`, so a listing row reads `status: rejected` beside `connectors[].state: ready`. Documented in the ADR note and `connectors.mdx`; should-fix on the design (clear the in-memory refusal on the first `2xx` after a re-materialization — no row is at stake there, unlike the stored case), or keep and accept the contradiction the UI sibling will have to render.
- Install-local `credentialNote` names the PUT route under a walled posture, where it refuses (acknowledged in the PR body). should-fix.
